The decay of a single atom follows an exponential distribution, which has the memoryless property. This means the probability of decay in a future time interval depends only on the length of that interval, not on how long the atom has already survived.

We are given that the probability of decay within 100 minutes is 32%, so:
P(T ≤ 100) = 0.32  ⇒  e^{-100λ} = 0.68.

We want the probability that the atom decays in the next 150 minutes, given it has already survived 50 minutes:
P(T ≤ 200 | T > 50) = P(T ≤ 150)   (by memoryless property, since 200 − 50 = 150).

Now compute P(T ≤ 150):
P(T ≤ 150) = 1 − e^{-150λ} = 1 − (e^{-100λ})^{1.5} = 1 − (0.68)^{1.5}.

Calculate (0.68)^{1.5}:
√0.68 ≈ 0.8246
0.68 × 0.8246 ≈ 0.5607
P(T ≤ 150) ≈ 1 − 0.5607 = 0.4393 ≈ 44%.

Answer: D
